title: NFC Review Card Vs QR Review Stand
summary: This comparison helps local businesses decide whether a tap-first review card or a scan-first QR stand fits the real customer moment better.
heroPoints: NFC and QR formats solve different in-person behavior patterns.
The best format depends on where the customer is standing, how quickly staff can prompt and which phones dominate.
Many businesses end up using a mixed format once the first pilot reveals real behavior.
imageAlt: NFC review card versus QR review stand

rows: Counter, checkout or handover moments where tap is natural
Fast interaction and premium physical feel
Needs phone compatibility and placement validation
Easy to understand visually and works without tap behavior
Can be ignored if placement is weak or the visual prompt is not strong

sections.title: What usually decides it
sections.intro: The best comparison pages remove one high-friction decision. These are the details that usually decide the first shortlist fastest.
bullets: Use the real customer handoff moment to decide whether tap or scan is more natural.
Treat phone mix, staff prompting and tabletop behavior as part of the format choice.
Keep the live review link and redirect ownership stable across whichever format wins.

sections.title: What to confirm before broader ordering
sections.intro: Use the first sample round to validate the assumptions below before the project expands into premium materials or large quantities.
bullets: Pilot one NFC and one QR format in the same real environment before scaling.
Measure actual customer response, not only staff preference.
Keep branding and premium materials secondary until the best interaction model is clear.

faq.question: Is NFC always better than QR for review collection?
faq.answer: No. NFC can feel faster and more premium, but QR can still perform better when the customer naturally scans at a static location.

faq.question: What should be tested first?
faq.answer: Test the actual customer interaction moment first: where the prompt appears, how staff introduces it and whether the phone behavior is reliable enough to scale.
